clues: This place sits in a high valley on a broad plateau in the middle of its land. A great lake once filled much of that valley floor.
Rain here falls most in the summer months, much of it in hard bursts with dense hail. Snow is so rare that it may not fall for many years.
This place was the seat of the Aztec Empire, and later it held the same role for a colony ruled from Spain. The king's man ruled from a palace on its main square.
An eagle sign told one people where to raise their island town on a lake in 1325. That island town, the Aztec capital, lies beneath the streets here today.
This place is the seat of the federal government, where the president and the lawmakers do their work. No other place in the land holds that role.
